verdict.line: You lose if you walk into a fresh Rupture or ignore Feast at low HP; you win if you convert the window after his Q is spent.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's kit is built around Q (Rupture), a 950-range skillshot that knocks up and slows on a 9s cooldown — he can zone and chip you from max range without ever entering your Q (Precision Protocol) auto range. The entire lane hinges on whether you can force or wait out that cooldown and convert with E (Hookshot) before he resets to max range. Camille vs Cho'Gath sits at 53.1% over 145 games with lane and solo-kill advantage both even, so this is a genuinely balanced skill matchup, not a lane you're favored or punished in by default.

theirWindow.what: He can poke you for free from 950 range with a knockup and slow attached — don't extend past your minions or try to force trades while this is loaded, since you have no way to avoid it at range.

yourWindow.when: right after he casts Q (whiffed or landed)
yourWindow.what: Rupture is on a 9s cooldown with no other escape, so this is your all-in window. Use E (Hookshot) to the nearest wall to close the gap with a knockup, then empowered Q auto into W (Tactical Sweep) for the slow and heal.

start.why: 66.7% win rate over 39 games. The physical-damage block and passive regen directly answer Vorpal Spikes chip and Rupture poke, which is the main way Cho'Gath damages you before level 6.

boots.why: 55.6% win rate over 108 games. Cho'Gath's entire damage profile (Rupture, Feral Scream, Feast) is magic, and the tenacity shortens his Rupture slow so you can close distance faster after dodging it.

core.why: 53.1% win rate as the start of the most-run path (36.8% pick). The move speed and empowered auto synergize directly with Q (Precision Protocol) for your all-in windows.
Sustained damage and healing on-hit lets you win extended trades once you're inside his spike range instead of getting worn down by Vorpal Spikes.
53.1% win rate on this full path over 32 games. The damage-over-time conversion keeps you alive through Feast's true damage burst at level 6+.

runes.keystoneWhy: 67.7% win rate on this page over the sampled games. The on-hit heal and bonus health directly offset the slow chip from Rupture and Vorpal Spikes across a long poke war.

summoners.why: 76.9% pick rate at 53.1% win rate. Ignite seals the all-in once you commit through his Q-down window, since Cho'Gath has no mobility to peel off after Feast's 175 range forces him in close. Flash+Teleport (57.1% win rate, 12.4% pick) is the higher-performing alternative if you'd rather prioritize wave control over securing early skirmishes.

playing.title: All-in only after his Q lands or whiffs
playing.detail: Rupture is on a 9s cooldown with no other way for him to disengage. The moment it's spent, use E (Hookshot) to a nearby wall to close the gap before he can reset to max range.

playing.title: Respect Feast once he hits 6
playing.detail: Feast devours at 175 range for high true damage and grows his max health on a kill (up to 6 stacks, 60s cooldown). Don't sit low HP in his face even if Rupture is down.

playing.title: Don't facetank extended auto trades
playing.detail: Vorpal Spikes fires passively off every one of his autos and hits everyone in front of him, so standing and auto-trading stacks extra damage on top of his base hits.

playing.title: Delay the Q recast when it's safe
playing.detail: Precision Protocol's second cast does significantly more damage if you wait between hits, but only delay when his Feral Scream (300 range cone, silence) isn't close enough to punish you standing still.

playing.title: Use R to finish, not to open
playing.detail: The Hextech Ultimatum dashes to him and anchors him in place — save it for after he's already committed past his Rupture rather than diving a fresh one.

playing.title: Path near walls on your side of lane
playing.detail: Hookshot only works off a nearby wall, so rotate your farming position to keep one in E range at all times for your post-Q engage window.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are our own tactical read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Although Cho’Gath’s (Q) is formidable, it is also easy to dodge. Try to fight him when (Q) is on cooldown to gain the upper hand.
